title: Private Deployment Quarter Runway: Initiative Thermometer & Runway Consolidation
creator: Liam Chen
description: Consolidate and validate the quarter-level roadmap for Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise features into a single operational runway (‘Runway Consolidation’). Produce an ‘Initiative Thermometer’ — a concise status view that translates engineering signals (capacity, stability, compatibility gates) into business-facing readiness levels for each tranche. Deliverables: reconciled milestone calendar, owner matrix, gating criteria, customer cohort mapping, and a communication plan for Sales/CS/Support.
acceptance_criteria: Single source-of-truth roadmap doc published in Confluence with owner and milestone gating criteria
Initiative Thermometer created and embedded in PI planning deck with clear green/amber/red rules based on objective signals
Cross-functional sign-off captured from Eng, Design, Security, and Support for each milestone
Runway has automated tracers to the runtime-1.18 and console-2026.03 releases where applicable
Rollout playbook draft for first 3 customer cohorts with rollback triggers and post-mortem template
milestones: 2026-03-18: Stakeholder kickoff — align objectives and success metrics
2026-03-26: Engineering capacity signal spec and acceptance thresholds (throughput/latency/failure budget)
2026-04-08: Thermometer UX + acceptance rules reviewed with Design and PM
2026-04-20: Compatibility gate matrix finalized (KMS/HSM, RBAC, network-topologies)
2026-04-30: Draft customer cohort rollout playbooks and support runbook
2026-05-10: Go/No-Go decision for tranche 1 and communication pack to GTM
risks: Late kernel/quantization compatibility causing sweep of model variants and added QA time
Customer network topologies require custom preflight that extends activation window
Insufficient Dedicated capacity reserves for tranche 1 leading to degraded SLA commitments
Cross-team misalignment on rollback criteria could delay canary/scale tests
notes: Trade-off: aggressive tranche cadence shortens time-to-value for customers but increases risk of compatibility regressions — mitigations include gated compatibility matrix and extended preflight for top 10 customers
Decision: use the existing console release channel (console-2026.03) for Thermometer UI rather than adding a separate feature flag to avoid rollout fragmentation
Consequence: will need one-off customer comms for teams on older runtime pins; include migration guidance in playbooks
